description: The bar chart illustrates the performance gain (+%) of three large vision-language models — GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and Qwen2-72B-VL — under two supervision conditions: “Strong Supervision” (represented by diagonally striped bars) and “Weak Supervision” (solid bars), as evaluated in the context of the VisuoThink framework for enhancing LVLM reasoning via multimodal tree search. The vertical axis, labeled “Performance Gain (+%)”, ranges from 0 to 30 in increments of 5, indicating the relative improvement in task performance. For GPT-4o, strong supervision yields a performance gain of approximately 24.5%, while weak supervision results in about 5.5%. Claude-3.5-Sonnet shows a gain of roughly 9.5% under strong supervision and 3.5% under weak supervision. Qwen2-72B-VL achieves approximately 15% gain with strong supervision and 5.5% with weak supervision. Across all models, strong supervision consistently produces significantly higher performance gains than weak supervision, with GPT-4o benefiting the most under strong supervision and Claude-3.5-Sonnet showing the smallest absolute gains in both conditions. The bars are grouped by model along the horizontal axis, with each group containing two adjacent bars for direct comparison between supervision types.
